name: Teetly
about: Hi! I go by Teetly, and I am a first-year PhD student in Biomedical Informatics at Vanderbilt. Prior to my PhD, I worked in high-performance computing, particularly improving LLM performance in generating low-resource languages, and computational biology research along the lines of protein structure representation learning. I am currently working with Bennett Landman.

interests.title: Multimodal representation learning
interests.description: How can we integrate imaging data with clinical notes to get a patient-level understanding?

interests.title: Medical imaging
interests.description: Currently, I am working on causal synthesis models for dermatology.

news.text: Oral presentation on paper "Evaluating LLM Generated Task Codes" at the 31st HIPS workshop held at IPDPS.
Received funding: Schultz Foundation Travel Award and Lazarus Center Professional Development Fund.
Presented oral presentation "Fine Tuning Convergence Experiments with Large Language Models Trained on High Performance Computing Code" at Celebrating Collaborations at Smith College.
Presented poster "Encoding Essential Features in Protein Structure for Task Generalization" at RosettaCon.

projects.title: Evaluating LLM Generated Task Codes (HIPS Paper)
projects.description: Evaluating LLM-generated high-performance computing task codes, including runtime performance and scaling behavior across thread counts.

projects.title: Undergrad Honors Thesis: How Well Can LLMs Generate and Translate Code to Asynchronous Many-Task Runtimes?
projects.description: An investigation of large language models for generating and translating code to asynchronous many-task runtimes, including analysis of compilation, syntax, type, linker, and runtime errors.

projects.title: Encoding Essential Features in Protein Structure for Task Generalization (Rosetta Commons Poster)
projects.description: Exploring protein structure representation learning using graph and point cloud encodings, with an emphasis on feature selection and generalization to downstream prediction tasks.
